symbolic_lower_bound.argument: After the x-prefix is fixed to alpha in {0,1}^m, the residual future is AND_i(y_i=alpha_i). Distinct alpha yield 2^m distinct residual Boolean functions. Exact OBDD nodes cannot merge distinct residual functions, so the cut requires at least 2^m semantic states. EQ_m input size is O(m). Therefore grouped/numeric-order ROBDD representation is exponential on this family.
symbolic_lower_bound.scope: This refutes the fixed grouped/numeric order as a universal polynomial MK_FUTURE representation. It does not refute order-aware ROBDDs or other representation languages.

order_aware_escape.discovery: A deterministic clause-pair detector finds every equivalence pair and constructs the interleaved order without truth-table/oracle access.
order_aware_escape.claim_scope: Family-specific polynomial representation/discovery only; not universal.

lineage.signature: m=13 reproduces 24573 grouped vs 39 interleaved nodes
lineage.novelty_rule: Do not count the rediscovered numerical signature as independent novelty; count R1 as a new integration of that barrier into MK_FUTURE/BCEG complexity accounting.

post_result_shift: Semantic future congruence is no longer the immediate ROBDD problem. Representation grammar/order is the bottleneck: exact future interfaces can be exponentially large under one representation and linear under another.
R2_objective: Attack functions/CNF families where OBDD remains large across all or broad order classes, and test whether a frozen exact representation portfolio can switch languages while preserving future-equivalence and charged discovery costs.
